business_scope.primary_industry_name: Multi-Jurisdictional Commercial Arbitration and Asset Tracing

Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement between Samoa and New Zealand (in force, applied by Order in Council)

Double Taxation Convention between Samoa and Norway

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended, including the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2017 and the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2020 providing for beneficial ownership registration and UBO filing; Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (Samoa No. 17 of 2007), as amended by the Money Laundering Prevention (Amendment) Act 2013 and the Money Laundering Prevention (Amendment) Act 2021; Terrorism Suppression Act 2002; the Financial Intelligence Unit established and empowered under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007; SIFA Beneficial Ownership Filing Regulations 2019; International Companies (Registered Agent and Registered Office) Regulations; and the AML/CFT Prescribed Obligations and Beneficial Ownership Rules issued by the Samoa International Finance Authority and the Samoan Financial Intelligence Unit.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, the licensed Samoan registered agent and its AML/CFT compliance officer must perform real-time screening of every proposed director, shareholder, beneficial owner, signatory, and the principal litigator against the United Nations Security Council consolidated list and Samoa domestic terrorist designation list under the Terrorism Suppression Act 2002; the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list as a benchmark control; the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list where EU banking relationships are anticipated; the Financial Action Task Force public statements and high-risk jurisdiction lists; and applicable Politically Exposed Persons datasets from the World Bank and Samoan integrity authorities. PEP status automatically triggers enhanced due diligence requiring written evidence of source of wealth and source of funds, senior management approval for foreign PEPs, and ongoing transaction monitoring, all consistent with SIFA AML/CFT Guidelines and FATF Recommendations 10, 12, and 25.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) eServices Registry Portal – International Company Name Reservation Module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must be expressed in Latin script; Samoan and English are the official languages, and a name may be in either language. Non-Latin scripts, including Chinese characters, are not accepted in the statutory name field; any proposed non-Latin name must be transliterated into English or Samoan before filing, and that transliterated name is the only operative registered name. The statutory name must end with the word 'Limited' or its accepted abbreviation 'Ltd.' or otherwise comply with the International Companies Act 1987 suffix requirements. A parallel Chinese or Samoan trading name may be adopted by internal resolution for client branding, provided it is disclosed to the AML officer and does not appear on the Certificate of Incorporation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banker, Banking, Banking Business, Mutual, Building Society, Savings, Trust, Trustee, Trust Company
Insurance, Assurance, Reinsurance, Underwriter, Fund, Investment Fund, Securities, Broker, Exchange, Settlement, Deposit, Credit Union
Government, Ministry, Authority, Crown, Royal, Imperial, Commonwealth, State, Federal, National, Municipal
Chamber of Commerce, University, College, Institute, Academy, Society, Association

Law, Legal, Litigation, Arbitration, Mediation, Attorney, Barrister, Solicitor, Counsel, Advocate — where the name implies provision of legal services, prior ministerial or Law Practitioners Committee approval and a statutory legal-services license are required
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be extended once for an additional 30 days upon payment of the gazetted extension fee through the SIFA portal. If the Registrar refuses a proposed name, the licensed registered agent may file an administrative appeal with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 working days of the refusal, attaching the refusal notice, a completed name-clearance request, any legal opinion on the permissibility of the name, and a written submission addressing the grounds of refusal. The Registrar must render a written decision within 21 working days. If the refusal is sustained, a further appeal may be filed with the Minister of Commerce, Industry and Labour within 15 working days, with a final decision expected within 30 working days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not permissible as the statutory registered office of a Samoa International Company. The company must maintain a physical registered office in Samoa, which is normally the physical suite of the licensed registered agent, for service of process and statutory records. Remote or virtual administrative support such as mail forwarding, digital correspondence, and cloud-based file hosting may be used for operational convenience, but the statutory address must remain the registered agent's Samoan physical office; any separate 'virtual office' marketed as the business address must be approved in writing by the registered agent and clearly identified as non-statutory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: For a low-risk international company in the commercial litigation services category, the quantified annual likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection by SIFA or the Financial Intelligence Unit is assessed at 10-15%, with inspections directed principally at the licensed registered agent's records and premises rather than the offshore entity's foreign administrative location; the risk increases to approximately 25-30% if the company is selected for a SIFA compliance review or if adverse media or transaction monitoring flags arise.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), ss 5-9 (incorporation, memorandum and articles, certificate of incorporation); International Companies (Amendment) Act 2018; Samoa International Financial Services Authority Act 2016; SIFSA (Fees) Regulations 2011; Business Licences Act 1998; Law Practitioners Act 2014, Part X (Foreign Legal Consultants)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Office of the Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 (Application for Incorporation), executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, and Declaration of Compliance filed under sections 5-9 of the International Companies Act 1987
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital; at least one issued share is required and may remain unpaid; no statutory escrow, capital deposit, or verification requirement applies to an International Company under the International Companies Act 1987
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers' application for the subscription and allotment of ordinary shares in the share capital of the Company be and is hereby approved and accepted. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office and main business address of the Company be established at [Registered Office Address], Apia, Samoa, and that such address be filed with the Registrar of International Companies. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Director Name] be appointed as the first director and [Secretary Name] as the first corporate secretary, with full authority to execute all statutory filings, open corporate bank and client IOLTA trust accounts, procure the Foreign Legal Consultant Certificate and relevant business licences, and bind the Company in ordinary commercial matters. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Memorandum and Articles of Association be adopted in their present form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Obtain Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA), Name Reservation Desk, Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed names via SIFSA's registry portal or in person at the Apia office, each name ending with 'Limited' or 'Ltd.'; pay the prescribed name search and reservation fee; obtain written clearance before filing. Restricted words (Bank, Trust, Insurance, Finance) require prior written consent of SIFSA.
required_dossiers: Name Reservation Application Form
Copy of proposed director or subscriber identification document
Name search and reservation fee receipt (US$25)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as undesirable or too similar to an existing name, file written representations via the licensed registered agent and propose an altered name; SIFSA must respond within 5 business days of the objection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appoint Licensed Registered Agent and Execute Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFSA-licensed International Company Service Provider / Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a SIFSA-licensed registered agent to provide the statutory registered office in Samoa; prepare, review and execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association, the Registered Agent Agreement, and the Beneficial Ownership Schedule; complete all KYC documentation for shareholders, directors, and the ultimate beneficial owner.
required_dossiers: SIFSA-licensed Registered Agent Agreement
Memorandum and Articles of Association (draft and execution copies)
KYC pack: certified copies of passports, recent utility bills, bank reference letter, and professional reference letter
Beneficial Ownership Schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Deficient KYC documentation is the most common query; cure by re-submitting notarially certified English translations or apostilled documents within 7 days of the agent's request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, SIFSA, Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 1 (Application for Incorporation), the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, and the statutory declarations of consent from the first director, secretary, and registered agent; pay the US$150 incorporation fee by bank wire or SIFSA trust account; obtain a stamped acknowledgment of filing.
required_dossiers: Completed Form 1 - Application for Incorporation
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Declaration of Compliance executed by a subscriber or registered agent
Consents to Act as Director, Secretary, and Registered Agent
Name clearance certificate
Incorporation fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a requisition or letter of defect, respond with amended or supplementary documents within 14 days; an extension of time may be requested by sworn affidavit, and re-application is available if the filing is rejected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation, Tax Identification Number, and Tax Exemption Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFSA Registry and Samoa Tax Administration (Ministry of Revenue)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the Certificate of Incorporation from SIFSA; apply to the Samoa Tax Administration for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) using Form IR01; submit the International Company exemption declaration confirming zero Samoan tax on offshore income; register for employer PAYE if local staff will be engaged.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Certified copy of Memorandum and Articles of Association
IR01 Tax Identification Number application form
International Company tax exemption declaration
Registered office confirmation letter from the licensed agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax exemption certificate is delayed, request an interim exemption letter from SIFSA; any adverse tax assessment may be protested in writing to the Ministry of Revenue within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate and Client Trust Accounts and Commence Regulatory Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank in Samoa (e.g., ANZ Samoa, BSL) and the Samoa Law Society / MCIL Business Licensing Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the incorporation pack to a licensed commercial bank to open a general operating account and a separate IOLTA client trust account; make the minimum opening deposit; concurrently file the Business Licence application with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry, Labour and Tourism and apply to the Samoa Law Society for a Foreign Legal Consultant Certificate if non-resident counsel will practise through the Company.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and constitution
Director KYC and beneficial ownership declarations
Bank account application and IOLTA trust account undertaking
Business Licence application form
Foreign Legal Consultant Certificate application (qualifications, certificate of good standing, professional indemnity insurance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank enhanced due diligence is triggered, provide a source-of-wealth declaration and a client structure chart; if the Business Licensing Division queries the application, submit a clarifying cover letter within 14 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry, Labour and Tourism (MCIL) Business Licensing Division, in conjunction with the Samoa Law Society and the Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence (Business Licences Act 1998) and Foreign Legal Consultant Certificate (Law Practitioners Act 2014, Part X)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 1 - Exempt from Full EIA; Registration Only (office-based professional services with no manufacturing, industrial discharge, or significant environmental footprint)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office wastewater to municipal sewer network per Samoa Water Authority Trade Waste Bylaws; zero VOC or stack emissions; solid waste segregation and disposal per Waste Management Act 2010; fit-out construction subject to PUMA building permit conditions and fire safety standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Clearance Certificate issued by the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA) upon annual inspection; structural load and occupancy clearance for the leased premises by the Ministry of Works, Transport and Infrastructure (MWTI); occupational health and safety registration and workplace clearance under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013 with Accident Compensation Corporation (Samoa) worker coverage certification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Ministry for Revenue (MoR); official e-services portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Samoa International Company (IC), no TIN/VAGST ID is required for offshore business because the IC enjoys a statutory tax-exempt zone classification. The standard procedure is for the registered agent to apply to the MoR for a Certificate of Tax Exemption using the agent authorization and the IC's Certificate of Incorporation; the MoR issues a tax-exempt certificate within 5 working days. If the IC carries on taxable activities in Samoa (e.g., local litigation support), it must apply for a TIN via Form IR-01 to the MoR Registrar, attaching the registered agent letter, director's passport copy, and certificate of registered office, and will then be issued a tax identifier and VAGST registration eligibility.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election or hybrid mismatch election exists in Samoa. Under the International Companies Act 1988, a foreign-owned IC may elect to maintain tax-exempt status by limiting its business to offshore activities; any decision to become a domestic company under the Companies Act 2001 or to be treated as a resident company for income tax purposes terminates the exempt status. Such election must be made in writing to the Registrar of International Companies and to the MoR Commercial Tax Division and is irrevocable for the remaining tax year.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 of taxable supplies in Samoa during any consecutive 12-month period
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API mandate, or digital stamping is currently in force. Taxpayers may issue electronic or paper invoices; VAGST returns must be filed online through the MoR e-services portal. The MoR does not require pre-approval of invoice numbering, but all invoices must contain the supplier's TIN, the words 'Tax Invoice', the date, description, GST amount, and tax-exclusive value.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to exported goods and to services supplied to a non-resident client who is outside Samoa at the time of supply and who receives the economic benefit outside Samoa. Cross-border commercial litigation and arbitration services provided from the Samoa IC to overseas principals are zero-rated if no part of the services is performed in Samoa, no land or goods in Samoa are involved, and the fees are paid from non-Samoan accounts. The supplier must obtain and preserve documentary evidence within 90 days after supply.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If zero-rating is claimed without the required export documentation or foreign inward remittance within 180 days, the supply is re-characterized as taxable at 15%, and a late assessment may be raised. Penalties include a tax shortfall penalty of 100% of the understated VAGST, a monthly late-payment penalty of 1.5% (minimum WST 100), and an 8% per annum interest charge. Fraudulent or negligent zero-rating claims are subject to civil penalties up to WST 100,000 and criminal prosecution under the Tax Administration Act 2004, with imprisonment up to three years; MoR may claw back refunds for six years and suspend the IC's tax-exempt certificate.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), also designated as the Exchange Control Authority under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, with the Minister of Finance retaining residual exchange control powers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan tālā (WST) is partially convertible. Current account transactions, including trade payments and ordinary profit repatriation by non-resident license holders, are generally permitted subject to CBS-approved exchange control forms and supporting documentation. Capital account transactions, especially capital injections, overseas investments, and offshore borrowings by resident entities, require prior CBS approval or an authorized dealer's exchange control compliance. For International Company structures, the Foreign Sales Corporation and International Companies Acts provide exemptions, but practical convertibility is administered through commercial banks as authorized dealers. Profit and capital outflows for non-resident shareholders are permitted upon proof of taxed/exempt status, audited financials, and absence of domestic liabilities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Samoa requires exporters to repatriate export proceeds to Samoa within 90 days of shipment unless a specific exemption is granted by the Central Bank of Samoa. The proceeds must be offered for conversion into WST through an authorized dealer unless the exporter holds an approved foreign currency retention account. Conversion of retained foreign currency above the statutory limit is subject to CBS approval. For International Companies whose export activities are carried on outside Samoa, the surrender rule may be relaxed, but the default statutory timeline and mandatory conversion ratio remain 100% unless a CBS exemption or foreign currency account authorization is obtained.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Foreign Currency Trust Account (USD/WST)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Samoa is not a recognized market for offshore digital electronic money institutions. The Central Bank of Samoa does not issue EMI licenses, and foreign fintech EMIs are not recognized as authorized dealers for WST clearing or exchange control purposes. An International Company may maintain a non-resident EMI account for auxiliary fiat collection, but it cannot serve as the primary IOLTA trust or settlement rail for Samoan-regulated litigation finance. Legal constraints include absence of an EMI passporting regime, CBS restrictions on foreign exchange transactions without an authorized dealer, and the Samoan Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2019 imposing record-keeping and monitoring obligations on local custodians. A licensed offshore bank under the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) is more viable than a generic offshore EMI but still lacks domestic clearing access.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors are generally required to complete a physical or bank-approved video-identification interview. Practical enforcement by CBS-regulated commercial banks requires at least one director or the registered agent of the International Company to present photo identification and source-of-funds evidence to a bank representative. Remote onboarding is limited to cases where the applicant maintains a pre-existing credit relationship with the bank's Samoa branch, and even then officers may require a notarized power of attorney plus a sworn affidavit of identity. For IOLTA trust account activation, physical presence of the responsible litigation partner or a court-appointed trustee/registered agent is the prevailing market standard.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: International Company with nominee shareholders or bearer-share legacy structures incapable of establishing ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The 2025 beneficial ownership register, filed with the Samoa International Finance Authority; an organizational chart showing all natural-person UBOs; certified copies of share registers; correspondence from the registered agent confirming the in-country information access right; and a declaration from each nominee holder disclaiming beneficial entitlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: IOLTA trust account funded by third-party litigation donors or conditional fee arrangements originating outside Samoa.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed litigation funding agreements; client and funder bank references; source-of-funds statements from the funding originator's regulated bank; the underlying commercial litigation engagement letter; a breakdown of expected disbursements; and a CBS-compliant purpose description referencing the IOLTA/trust exemption.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-volume cross-border wire inflows and outflows inconsistent with the Low_Risk_Standard AML rating.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A transaction-level projection model with counterparty names, legal basis for each payment, and reconciliation to the underlying arbitration/tracing case files; a domestic agent appointment to maintain transaction records; and a signed AML compliance manual aligned with the Samoan AML/CFT Act and SIFA guidelines.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Samoa International Company does not hold a statutory license or registered-agent confirmation for cross-border commercial litigation activities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Certificate of Good Standing issued by SIFA; the ISIC 6910 business description in the annual return; a licensed lawyer's undertaking for professional oversight; and evidence that the Samoa office, if any, is not rendering local legal services in violation of the Samoa Law Practitioners Act.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's regulated bank to the Samoa International Company's WST or USD operating account at an authorized dealer. The wire instruction must state the purpose code 'Capital Injection / Direct Investment' and identify the legal entity as 'WS_IC (International Company No. XXX)'. The bank will require the CBS Exchange Control form for capital transactions, a board resolution authorizing the contribution, and a certificate from the registered agent verifying that the entity is an International Company exempt from minimum capital requirements. Funds received in foreign currency may be credited to an external WST-denominated or USD-denominated account only after exchange control approval or a standing foreign currency retention authorization.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for the cross-border commercial litigation chambers are cleared via SWIFT MT103 for direct payments to counterparties, expert witnesses, arbitral institutions, and asset-tracing agents. SWIFT MT202 is used for bank-to-bank settlement where the beneficiary is a financial institution. Commercial letters of credit (MT700) are permissible only if the litigation structure undertakes tangible trade or settlement collateral obligations, which is unusual; standard IOLTA disbursements are executed by wire transfer. All outbound payments must use CBS-compliant purpose codes indicating 'Legal Services', 'Arbitration Fees', or 'Professional Fees', and disbursements from an IOLTA account require a written client instruction, a payment memorandum, and reconciliation entries against the client matter ledger. Hard-copy bank drafts may be used for recipients without SWIFT connectivity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward foreign exchange contracts traded with an authorized dealer in Samoa for WST/USD and WST/AUD exposures up to one year
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referenced to WST offered by offshore dealing desks outside Samoa, subject to CBS exchange control approval for non-resident hedging
Spot foreign exchange transactions at the authorized dealer's indicative rate for same-day settlement
Bank-guaranteed currency swaps for multi-currency escrow balances, requiring prior CBS capital account authorization
Premium-paying currency options on USD/WST and AUD/WST, where permitted by the licensed bank's derivatives governance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Annual License Fee (confirmation of company particulars)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge on the annual fee; if fees remain unpaid for 3 consecutive months, the Registrar may issue a strike-off notice and, if not remedied within 30 days, strike the company off the International Companies Register and forfeit its assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Economic Substance Confirmation/Declaration (where the IC carries on a relevant activity, e.g., legal services)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, with coordination by the Samoa Revenue and Customs Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the company's financial year, filed together with the annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a valid economic substance confirmation may result in financial penalties, revocation of the tax exemption certificate, and potentially cancellation of the company's registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Update of UBO Register (private filing with the registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Registered Agent in Samoa (statutory record-keeping; not a public filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of incorporation; any change in beneficial ownership must be reported within 14 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative default resulting in a mandatory report to the Registrar; persistent non-compliance may attract AML/CFT penalties against the company or its officers and may ground strike-off proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit applies to a tax-exempt Samoa International Company under the International Companies Act 2012; an audit is mandatory only for ICs licensed to carry on banking, insurance, or trust business, or where the company's articles of association expressly require it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Companies Act 2012 (statutory accounting records requirement); IFRS or equivalent recognized accounting framework for any voluntarily prepared financial statements. No obligation to file financial statements with the Registrar.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The IC is not required to file a public UBO return; it must maintain a confidential beneficial ownership register at the registered office and deliver a written annual confirmation to the licensed registered agent, updating any shareholding transfers and consequential ownership changes within 14 days. The register is accessible only to the Registrar and designated lawful authorities.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800–1,200 per annum (licensed registered agent and registered office combined)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required for audit-exempt IC; voluntary certified audit USD 3,000–6,000 per engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for International Companies (IC) under the International Companies Act 1988 (as amended); standard resident corporate rate is 27% under the Income Tax Act 2015.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies are wholly exempt from income tax, capital gains tax, dividend withholding tax, and stamp duty. No deemed profits or presumptive tax regime applies to ICs. Preferential deductions are irrelevant due to absolute tax exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No corporate income tax return is required for a tax-exempt International Company. Annual compliance is effected via the IC Annual Return (IC-AR) filed with the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is within 30 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation, or by 31 December for companies with a calendar-year registration anniversary, as notified by the Registrar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: legal name, IC number, date of incorporation, registered office address in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners must provide the IC registration number and Samoa registered agent's address; no local tax identification number is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered agent details: name, address, and license number of the Samoa-licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered agent must be a Samoa-licensed trustee or corporate services provider; non-resident parties cannot act as registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors and shareholders: names, nationality, percentage shareholding, and appointment dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors and shareholders may be listed without Samoan tax identification; certified passport copies are sufficient.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compliance declaration: certification that the IC has not carried on business with Samoan residents or owned Samoa land, maintaining its exempt status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The declaration is signed by the registered agent; non-resident officers must ensure factual accuracy to avoid penal liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late submission of the IC-AR incurs a late fee of WST 100 per month or part thereof, subject to a maximum of WST 1,000. Failure to file may result in the Registrar striking off the company, forfeiting assets to the Samoa Government, and the loss of limited liability protection.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for International Companies. Standard Samoa domestic dividend withholding tax is 15% under the Income Tax Act 2015, but this is wholly disapplied for IC distributions under the International Companies Act exemption.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: As IC distributions suffer no Samoa withholding tax, treaty relief is generally unnecessary. If an IC voluntarily enters the standard tax regime or generates Samoan-source income without the exemption, treaty relief would require submission of the Samoa Ministry of Revenue withholding tax exemption form, along with a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty counterpart's revenue authority, and a supporting statement of beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For exempt International Companies, cross-border royalties and interest are paid without Samoa withholding tax. Under the standard Samoa Income Tax Act, non-resident recipients are subject to 15% withholding tax on Samoan-source interest and 15% on royalties; treaty rates may reduce these rates and are applied via the same TRC-based relief protocol.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No transfer pricing documentation thresholds are specifically gazetted for tax-exempt International Companies. As a prudent compliance standard, related-party cross-border transactions exceeding WST 5,000,000 in aggregate per fiscal year should be covered by contemporaneous local file and master file documentation, consistent with the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines incorporated by the Samoa Income Tax Act 2015.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) under the International Companies Amendment Act 2021 require every International Company carrying on a relevant activity (banking, financing, leasing, fund management, headquarters, holding, intellectual property, distribution, and service center) to demonstrate adequate substance in Samoa. This includes physical presence, qualified local employees, local board meetings, and substantial operational expenditure. Exempt companies must maintain a simple holding-company substance declaration. The Registrar of International Companies screens filings; non-compliance carries automatic penalties and possible deregistration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the International Company exemption to conceal Samoan-source taxable activities, such as providing commercial to Samoan residents or earning Samoan-source fees while claiming the IC exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imposition of the full corporate income tax rate of 27%, plus interest and a penalty of up to 200% of the tax shortfall under the Samoa Income Tax Act 2015. The IC's exempt status may be retroactively revoked and the company may be struck off the International Companies Register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly signed false declarations face criminal liability under the Crimes Act 2013, with penalties including imprisonment up to 7 years, fines up to WST 250,000, and a travel ban. Civil restitution orders may pierce the corporate veil, holding directors jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating in a high-risk sector, such as cross-border commercial litigation and asset tracing, without maintaining a local office, local management, or Samsung-real economic footprint in Samoa, while claiming tax-exempt status in a treaty network.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Mandatory penalty of WST 250,000, deregistration of the International Company, and forfeiture of assets under the Economic Substance Regulations. The Minister of Revenue may also impose annual substance reporting requirements and deny benefits to the entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and registered agents are personally liable for substances declarations; false certification attracts fines and up to 3 years' imprisonment. A court may order directorial disqualification and a travel ban for failure to cooperate with the Ministry of Revenue.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the IC to move funds into IOLTA trust accounts or wire payments without adequate client due diligence, particularly in cross-border commercial litigation where third-party fund flows may conceal origin or beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Offences under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2021 (Samoa) carry penalties up to WST 1,000,000 for entities and WST 500,000 for individuals, plus asset seizure and freezing orders. The International Company may be wound up by the Financial Intelligence Unit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and registered agents are personally exposed to criminal prosecution. Convictions may result in up to 10 years' imprisonment, personal travel bans, and extension of restitution orders beyond corporate assets to personal property obtained from the illicit activity.
